question: If the heart's natural pacemaker fails, what keeps the heart beating?
answer: Backups lower down, each slower than the last. Cells around the AV node, the gate to the lower chambers, fire on their own at about 40 to 60 a minute; the ventricles' fibres at about 20 to 40. Normally the fastest site sets every beat. A slower drummer takes over when the lead stops.
move: The fastest voice in a system can hide the backups waiting behind it.
reference: Katz, Physiology of the Heart, 5th edition, Lippincott Williams & Wilkins, 2011
